key_insight: Hyperspectral imaging can separate and map donor/acceptor distributions in roll-to-roll slot-die coated organic photovoltaic active layers in real time.
engineering_relevance: This enables inline quality control for scalable organic solar-cell manufacturing, helping detect coating nonuniformity before devices are finished.
method: Inline hyperspectral camera on a roll-to-roll slot-die coating line
Multivariate curve resolution to resolve P3HT and OIDTBR spatial contributions
Spectral fitting of P3HT absorbance to estimate exciton bandwidth and aggregation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reliable spatial separation of donor and acceptor signals and successful mapping of exciton bandwidth across the coated films.
watch_item: Deployment depends on robust spectral calibration and model stability under production-line variations in speed, lighting, and film thickness.
paper_title: Hyperspectral imaging for inline quality monitoring of roll-to-roll slot-die coated organic photovoltaic active layers
